Fact.Name: Gave cash to qualifying charities
Fact.Description: #45 gate. Cash or check gifts to a §170(b)(1)(A) charity, not to a 509(a)(3) supporting organization and not to a donor-advised fund (§170(p)(1)-(2)).

Fact.Name: Cash gifts to qualifying charities
Fact.Description: #45: total cash or check gifts made in the tax year to qualifying charities, excluding gifts to supporting organizations and donor-advised funds (§170(p)). Noncash gifts and carryovers ((d)(1)) don't count.

Fact.Name: Qualifying cash gifts ($0 when the gate is no or unanswered)
Fact.Description: #45: an unanswered gate counts as $0 so existing returns stay complete.

Fact.Name: §170(p) cap
Fact.Description: #45: "$1,000 ($2,000 in the case of a joint return)", IRC §170(p) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/170), as amended by P.L. 119-21 §70424, effective for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025. MFS, single, head of household, and qualifying surviving spouse get $1,000.

Fact.Name: Line 12f amount if the standard deduction is taken
Fact.Description: #45: lesser of the qualifying cash gifts, the §170(p) cap, and the 60% cash limit of §170(b)(1)(G)(i) ("does not exceed the excess of (I) 60 percent of the taxpayer's contribution base"; contribution base = AGI, §170(b)(1)(H), no NOL carryback in scope). §170(p) computes the deduction "without regard to" (b)(1)(I), so the 0.5% floor of §170(b)(1)(I) does not apply here; the floor applies only to itemized gifts (Schedule A line 13, scheduleA.xml). It is also computed without regard to (b)(1)(G)(ii) carryovers and (d)(1), so nothing carries over from or to this deduction. Not gated by itemizing, so /itemizesDeductions can compare Schedule A with standard + this amount without a cycle.

Fact.Name: Charitable contribution deduction for non-itemizers (Form 1040 line 12f)
Fact.Description: #45: $0 when itemizing (§170(p) applies only "if the individual does not elect to itemize"), so it never stacks with Schedule A line 11/13. Added to /totalDeductions (line 14) next to line 12e; it is separate from Schedule 1-A (line 13a), so future Schedule 1-A deductions add alongside it.
